question: An endocervical swab is performed and nucleic acid amplification testing via polymerase chain reaction is conducted. It is positive for Chlamydia trachomatis and negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Chlamydia trachomatis infection -> requires antibiotic treatment -> 90% CHAIN: Positive for Chlamydia trachomatis -> negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae -> treat Chlamydia trachomatis infection -> 85% CHAIN: Positive for Chlamydia trachomatis -> negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae -> consider dual therapy for possible co-infection -> 80% CHAIN: Positive for Chlamydia trachomatis -> negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae -> treat with antibiotics effective against Chlamydia trachomatis -> 85% CHAIN: Positive for Chlamydia trachomatis -> negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae -> consider azithromycin for Chlamydia trachomatis -> 90%
analysis: Chlamydia trachomatis infection is treated with antibiotics such as azithromycin or doxycycline. As the patient is positive for Chlamydia trachomatis and negative for Neisseria gonorrhoeae, the most appropriate pharmacotherapy would be to treat with a single dose of oral azithromycin.
